review.summary: Mercedes lead the constructors' championship after 17 rounds on 578 points, with 11 wins and 22 podiums. Andrea Kimi Antonelli heads the drivers' standings ahead of team-mate George Russell, who is second.
review.lastRace: At the Singapore Grand Prix, Antonelli finished third from fourth on the grid to take a podium and 15 points, while Russell recovered from grid 19 to finish ninth for two points.

review.summary: Ferrari are second after 17 rounds on 444 points, with two wins and 11 podiums. Lewis Hamilton leads the pair, third in the drivers' standings ahead of team-mate Charles Leclerc, who is fifth.
review.lastRace: Charles Leclerc finished second from second on the grid for a podium and 18 points at the Singapore Grand Prix, while Lewis Hamilton started third to finish sixth for eight points.

review.summary: McLaren are third after 17 rounds on 339 points, with two wins and seven podiums. Lando Norris leads the drivers' standings ahead of team-mate Oscar Piastri; Norris is sixth while Piastri sits seventh.
review.lastRace: At the Singapore Grand Prix, Lando Norris finished fourth from fifth for 12 points and Oscar Piastri followed home fifth from sixth for 10 points.

review.summary: Red Bull are fourth after 17 rounds on 332 points, with two wins and 11 podiums. Max Verstappen leads the drivers' standings at fourth, well clear of Isack Hadjar in eighth; Liam Lawson is ninth.
review.lastRace: Max Verstappen took victory from pole at the Singapore Grand Prix for 25 points, while Isack Hadjar climbed from grid 22 to finish tenth for a point.

review.summary: RB F1 Team are fifth after 17 rounds on 100 points, with no wins and no podiums. Arvid Lindblad leads the team's drivers at eleventh with 38 points, while Yuki Tsunoda is twentieth.
review.lastRace: At the Singapore Grand Prix, Liam Lawson finished seventh from eighth for six points, but Arvid Lindblad was lapped and finished fifteenth without scoring.

review.summary: Alpine are sixth after 17 rounds on 68 points, with no wins and no podiums. Pierre Gasly leads the pair at tenth with 41 points, ahead of team-mate Franco Colapinto, who is twelfth.
review.lastRace: Pierre Gasly was lapped and finished eleventh from seventh for no points at the Singapore Grand Prix, while Franco Colapinto retired from grid 15.

review.summary: Haas are seventh after 17 rounds on 30 points, with no wins and no podiums. Oliver Bearman leads the team's drivers at thirteenth with 23 points, ahead of Esteban Ocon, who is sixteenth.
review.lastRace: At the Singapore Grand Prix both Haas cars were lapped: Oliver Bearman finished twelfth from eleventh and Esteban Ocon was thirteenth from twelfth, neither scoring.

review.summary: Audi are eighth after 17 rounds on 23 points, with no wins and no podiums. Nico Hülkenberg leads the pair at fourteenth with 13 points, ahead of team-mate Gabriel Bortoleto, who is fifteenth.
review.lastRace: Nico Hülkenberg finished eighth from tenth for four points at the Singapore Grand Prix, but Gabriel Bortoleto retired from grid 14 without scoring.

review.summary: Williams are ninth after 17 rounds on 12 points, with no wins and no podiums. Carlos Sainz leads the team's drivers at eighteenth with 7 points, ahead of Alexander Albon, who is nineteenth.
review.lastRace: Carlos Sainz was lapped and finished fourteenth from thirteenth for no points at the Singapore Grand Prix, while Alexander Albon retired from grid 16.

review.summary: Aston Martin are tenth after 17 rounds on 7 points, with no wins and no podiums. Fernando Alonso leads the pair at seventeenth with all of the team's points, ahead of Lance Stroll, who is twenty-first.
review.lastRace: Fernando Alonso was lapped and finished sixteenth from twentieth for no points at the Singapore Grand Prix, while Lance Stroll retired from grid 21.

review.summary: Cadillac are eleventh after 17 rounds on 0 points, with no wins and no podiums. Valtteri Bottas is twenty-second and Sergio Pérez twenty-third in the drivers' standings; neither has scored.
review.lastRace: At the Singapore Grand Prix, Sergio Pérez was lapped and finished seventeenth from seventeenth, while Vltteri Bottas was nineteenth from eighteenth; neither scored a point.

review.summary: Aprilia lead after 17 rounds with 8 wins and 31 podiums. Jorge Martin heads the championship in first, Marco Bezzecchi is third and Raul Fernandez seventh — four Aprilia riders inside the top seven. At Indonesia round 17 Marco Bezzecchi won, with Raul Fernandez second, Jorge Martin third and Ai Ogura fourth for a clean sweep of the front four.
review.lastRace: Marco Bezzecchi won the Grand Prix of Indonesia, round 17, taking 25 points. Raul Fernandez was second (20), Jorge Martin third (16) and Ai Ogura fourth (13), giving Aprilia a clean sweep of the first four places.

review.summary: Ducati are second after 17 rounds with 7 wins and 13 podiums. Marc Marquez sits second in the standings, ahead of Fabio Di Giannantonio sixth and Alex Marquez eighth. Francesco Bagnaia ninth and Fermin Aldeguer tenth extend a broader spread of scorers, though their win and podium tallies remain behind the leaders.
review.lastRace: At Indonesia round 17, Marc Marquez finished sixth taking 10 points, with Alex Marquez seventh (9) and Fabio Di Giannantonio eighth (8). Franco Morbidelli was fourteenth (2), while Francesco Bagnaia and Fermin Aldeguer did not finish.

review.summary: KTM are third after 17 rounds with 2 wins and 7 podiums. Pedro Acosta is their best-placed rider at fifth, clear of Enea Bastianini eleventh and Brad Binder thirteenth. Maverick Viñales twenty-second, Pol Espargaro twenty-fifth and Jonas Folger twenty-ninth contribute little.
review.lastRace: At Indonesia round 17, Pedro Acosta finished fifth taking 11 points, with Enea Bastianini tenth (6) and Brad Binder eleventh (5). Maverick Viñales completed the race fourteenth but did not score.

review.summary: Honda are fourth after 17 rounds with no wins and no podiums. Luca Marini is their best-placed rider at twelfth, ahead of Diogo Moreira fifteenth and Johann Zarco seventeenth. Joan Mir eighteenth sits above a tail that includes Somkiat Chantra, Takaaki Nakagami and two further riders.
review.lastRace: At Indonesia round 17, Luca Marini finished twelfth taking 4 points, with Johann Zarco thirteenth (3). Diogo Moreira completed the race sixteenth but did not score.

review.summary: Yamaha are fifth after 17 rounds with no wins and no podiums. Fabio Quartararo leads the squad at fourteenth, ahead of Jack Miller nineteenth and Alex Rins twentieth. Toprak Razgatlioglu twenty-first and Augusto Fernandez twenty-fourth sit well clear.
review.lastRace: At Indonesia round 17, Fabio Quartararo finished ninth taking 7 points, with Alex Rins fifteenth (1). Toprak Razgatlioglu and Jack Miller both did not finish.

review.summary: They lead the championship with 288 points after 17 rounds, four wins and ten podiums. Evans leads the pair in third on 160, ahead of Da Costa in sixth on 128.
review.lastRace: Evans finished fourth from fifth on the grid to take 12 points, while Da Costa dropped back from ninth to fifteenth without scoring.

review.summary: Second on 271 points after 17 rounds with four wins and eight podiums. Wehrlein tops their drivers in first with 169, well clear of Müller in ninth on 102.
review.lastRace: Both scored nothing — Müller faded from fourth to twelfth and Wehrlein slipped from third to fourteenth.

review.summary: Third on 252 points after 17 rounds, two wins and seven podiums. Mortara leads the pairing in fifth on 137, ahead of De Vries in seventh on 115.
review.lastRace: A strong result — De Vries took second from the front row for 21 points and Mortara completed a Mahindra one-two with third from second.

review.summary: Fourth on 229 points after 17 rounds with two wins and seven podiums. Dennis is their stronger driver in second on 164, well ahead of Drugovich in fourteenth on 65.
review.lastRace: Neither scored — Drugovich finished thirteenth from eleventh and Dennis dropped to eighteenth from sixteenth.

review.summary: Fifth on 182 points after 17 rounds with one win and six podiums. Cassidy leads the pair in eighth on 114, ahead of Vergne in twelfth on 68.
review.lastRace: Both scored — Cassidy took sixth from seventh for 8 points and Vergne finished seventh from twelfth for 6.

review.summary: Sixth on 157 points after 17 rounds with one win and six podiums. Rowland is clearly their lead driver in fourth on 137, far ahead of Nato in nineteenth on 20.
review.lastRace: Rowland recovered to ninth from seventeenth for 3 points, while Nato finished tenth from nineteenth for 1.

review.summary: Seventh on 152 points after 17 rounds with no wins but two podiums. Buemi leads the pair in tenth on 97, ahead of Eriksson in sixteenth on 55.
review.lastRace: Buemi climbed to fifth from tenth for 10 points, while Eriksson failed to finish from fifteenth on the grid without scoring.

review.summary: Eighth on 128 points after 17 rounds with one win and three podiums. Martí leads narrowly in thirteenth on 66, just ahead of Ticktum in fifteenth on 62.
review.lastRace: Martí scored four from thirteenth to eighth, while Ticktum dropped back from eighth to sixteenth without points.

review.summary: Ninth on 91 points after 17 rounds with one win and one podium. Barnard leads their pair in eleventh on 68, well ahead of Günther in eighteenth on 23.
review.lastRace: A win — Barnard took first from sixth for 25 points, while Günther finished eleventh from fourteenth without scoring.

Pritto sits thirty-first with zero points from 17 rounds, off the podium and behind all his Ducati teammates including Bagnaia, Aldeguer and Morbidelli.

Bastianini sits eleventh with 122 points from 17 rounds and no wins or podiums, trailing teammate Acosta by 136. He finished his Indonesian Grand Prix tenth for six points.
Binder is thirteenth with 104 points from 17 rounds and no podiums, behind teammate Acosta. He finished his Indonesian Grand Prix eleventh for five points.
22nd on 12 points from 17 rounds, with no wins or podiums. He is KTM's top rider, ahead of Espargaro (25th, 5) and Folger (29th, 0). At the Indonesian GP he finished 17th without scoring.
25th on 5 points from 17 rounds, with no wins or podiums. He trails team-mate Viñales (22nd, 12) but leads Folger (29th, 0).

12th on 108 points from 17 rounds, with no wins or podiums. He is Honda's leading rider, clear of Moreira (15th, 74) and Zarco (17th, 51). At the Indonesian GP he finished 12th, scoring 4.

17th on 51 points from 17 rounds, with no wins or podiums. Behind Marini (12th, 108) and Moreira (15th, 74), but ahead of Mir (18th, 33). He finished 13th at the Indonesian GP, scoring 3.
18th on 33 points from 17 rounds, with no wins or podiums. He trails Zarco (17th, 51) but leads team-mate Chantra (26th, 3).
26th on 3 points from 17 rounds, with no wins or podiums. He sits behind team-mate Mir (18th, 33) in the Honda order.

Aleix Espargaro sits 32nd after 17 rounds on 0 points with no wins or podiums, at the back of the Honda group. Teammates Takaaki Nakagami (3) and Cal Crutchlow also lack points this season.

review.summary: Twentieth in the standings with just 3 points from 17 rounds and no wins or podiums, trailing team-mate Lucas Di Grassi. His London E-Prix saw him finish seventeenth after starting eighteenth on the grid for no points.

Max Verstappen won the Singapore Grand Prix from pole for Red Bull, holding off Charles Leclerc of Ferrari, who set the fastest lap, with Andrea Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes on the podium. The front three finished within 25 seconds of each other, but the field spread out behind them, several cars being lapped. Isack Hadjar recovered from grid 22 to finish tenth and take a point.
highlights: Isack Hadjar climbed twelve places from grid 22 to finish tenth and score a point.
Charles Leclerc set the fastest lap of the race for Ferrari.
George Russell recovered from grid 19 to finish ninth and take two points.

review.summary: Marco Bezzecchi won for Aprilia Racing, holding off Raul Fernandez of SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team who took second, with team-mate Jorge Martin third. The front four were then Pedro Acosta fifth for KTM, Marc Marquez sixth for Ducati, Alex Marquez seventh and Fabio Di Giannantonio eighth. Two retirements stood out: Francesco Bagnaia and Fermin Aldeguer both stopped for Ducati, while Toprak Razgatlioglu and Jack Miller retired early for Yamaha. No fastest lap was recorded.
highlights: Marco Bezzecchi won the Grand Prix of Indonesia for Aprilia Racing, taking 25 points.
The podium held two Aprilia riders alongside Raul Fernandez of SuperFile Trackhouse in second place.
Two retirements shaped the race: Francesco Bagnaia and Fermin Aldeguer both stopped for Ducati.
Toprak Razgatlioglu and Jack Miller retired without points for Yamaha.

review.summary: Taylor Barnard of DS Penske won from sixth on the grid, holding off a Mahindra one-two as Nyck De Vries finished second and Edoardo Mortara third. The front row largely delivered — both starters made the podium — while Wehrlein (third) and Müller (fourth) faded to fourteenth and twelfth. Evans took the last paying spot in fourth.
highlights: Norman Nato made the biggest climb, rising from nineteenth on the grid to tenth for a point.
Taylor Barnard rose from sixth to win for DS Penske, taking the full 25 points.
Mahindra's Nyck De Vries and Edoardo Mortara started first and second and finished second and third for a one-two.
